title: Thread-safe cache design
idea: A thread-safe cache keeps its map and recency order consistent under many threads and makes concurrent misses for one key share a single load.

analogy.text: A shared answer board. Two people see a blank and both phone the expert. A note saying "calling now" makes the second person wait instead.
analogy.breaks: Threads may not see a note unless a thread-safe map holds it.

points: An LRU `get` reorders the list, so even reads need exclusive access.
One lock around the cache is simple and correct, but limits throughput.
Striping splits keys over several locked caches; eviction becomes per stripe.
Concurrent misses on one key should share one in-flight future, not reload.

hero.title: A cache stampede and its fix

messages.label: get user:42
messages.note: A misses: nothing is cached for this key yet.

messages.label: get user:42
messages.note: B misses too, before A has loaded anything.

messages.label: load user:42
messages.note: B loads the same row. With many readers, the database takes one query each.

messages.label: computeIfAbsent
messages.note: Fix, replaying the same two reads: A asks the map to create one in-flight future for the key.

messages.label: computeIfAbsent
messages.note: B finds the same future already there and waits on it.

messages.label: load once
messages.note: Only the future's task queries the database.

messages.label: row
messages.note: The row completes the future, and every waiting thread receives it.

code.title: Prove the stampede
code.caption: A barrier makes four threads look before any of them loads, so the duplicate loads show up every run.

walk.text: Run the same four-reader race twice: plain check, then single flight.
A load counter, two maps, and a barrier for four threads.
Only the first `computeIfAbsent` creates the future; the rest join it.
Plain version: all four see a miss, wait, then all four load.
Join every thread before reading the counter, so the output is stable.

code.title: One lock, LRU inside
code.caption: Four threads hammer a five-entry LRU behind one lock. Every operation completes and the size stays at capacity. LinkedHashMap alone is not thread-safe, and access order makes every get a write.

walk.text: Four workers each run 25,000 operations over ten keys.
A miss loads the value; a hit checks it belongs to its key.
After joining, print the operation count, wrong values and final size.
Inside sits the access-ordered LinkedHashMap from the previous page.
`get` takes the same lock as `put`, because a read moves the key.

pitfalls: Never guard an LRU `get` with a read lock; it changes the order.
Do not run slow loads inside `computeIfAbsent`; store a future there instead.
Remove each future once it settles; keep finished values only in the bounded LRU.

quiz.q: What is the first line Stampede prints?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: The barrier lets all four threads see a miss before any loads. Each then loads, so the counter reaches four.

takeaway: Lock reads too in LRU, and let one thread load each missing key.
